about: The tracking plan (ADR 0036). Every feature asks which signal proves it is used and that it is worth it; every signal is here with the attributes it carries. Edit this file, then run `node tools/tracking-plan.mjs`: it writes docs/telemetry/tracking-plan.md and the frontend's event types. TrackingPlanTests holds the code to it at both ends.

features.name: Search
features.question: What share of typed searches finds nothing, and is it worse for agents than for people?
features.decision: Where the next relevance work goes: synonyms and golden-set queries for the empty ones, or the MCP tool's description if agents come back empty more often than people.

features.name: Browsing by category
features.question: Do people browse the taxonomy, or go straight to search?
features.decision: Whether the category pages earn their place in the navigation.

features.name: Product page
features.question: How do shoppers reach a product — a search, a category, the home page — and how many product views does a cart follow?
features.decision: Where discovery work goes: the search box, the taxonomy or the home page's rows.

features.name: Cart
features.question: How many carts never become an order, and whose?
features.decision: Whether abandonment work (a saved cart, a reminder) comes before checkout friction.

features.name: Promotions
features.question: What share of orders carries a discount?
features.decision: Whether the promotion engine's combination rules are worth extending, or promotions stay a handful of codes.

features.name: Checkout and payment
features.question: Why does a checkout fail to become an order: a stale screen, a changed price, a declined card, or a provider that did not answer?
features.decision: A stale screen or a price change is our copy and our cache; a decline is the shopper's; an unavailable provider is ours to retry. Each points at a different fix.

features.name: Order page
features.question: Do shoppers come back to follow an order?
features.gap: No decision depends on the answer: the page is the receipt, and it stays whatever the count is. A signal with no decision does not enter the plan.

features.name: Returns
features.question: Why do things come back?
features.decision: Wrong size and not-as-described are the product reasoning layer's case (phase 10); damaged and wrong item are the warehouse's.

features.name: Account and guest cart claim
features.question: Do guests sign in, and does their cart survive it?
features.decision: Whether guest checkout stays the default path.
features.gap: Not measured yet, and not planned: sign-in is the identity provider's, and the claim is one call with no screen of its own. Revisit when accounts do more than hold orders.

features.name: Review queue and publishing
features.question: Does the review queue move: how many drafts become products, and who approves them?
features.decision: Whether publishing needs bulk approval, and later whether the AI proposals of phase 10 are being approved or ignored.

features.name: Stock and reservations
features.question: How much held stock never becomes a sale?
features.decision: The hold's lifetime, and whether the expiry sweep the domain has a state for is worth building.

features.name: Catalogue import
features.question: Does an import bring products in?
features.gap: An import is an operator's batch, answered by its own result and its span; a counter would say what the result already says.

features.name: Back-office administration
features.question: Are the orders, returns, promotions, attributes, variants, stock and audit screens used?
features.decision: None at three roles and a handful of users.
features.gap: Every write they make is already an audit row with its actor (ListAuditEntries): that is their evidence, and a metric would count the same thing twice.

features.name: WebMCP
features.question: Do browser agents use the shop's WebMCP tools, which ones, and do they succeed?
features.decision: Which tools to keep, extend or drop; a high share of refusals means a tool's contract is wrong for an agent.

features.name: MCP server and UCP catalogue
features.question: Do external agents call the catalogue over MCP and UCP, which tools, and how often are they refused?
features.decision: Whether the agent checkout of phase 11 has agents waiting for it, and which binding to build it on first.

features.name: AI search layer
features.question: How often is a search answered without one of its AI stages, and how many product changes did the vector layer miss?
features.decision: Whether the AI stages can be on by default, which service to fix first, and when a reindex is due.

features.name: Outbox
features.question: Is eventual consistency still eventual?
features.decision: When a second worker replica, and the row locking it needs, is worth building.

events.name: webmcp_tool_invoked
events.description: A browser agent called one of the shop's WebMCP tools. Emitted with actor `webmcp`.

tool.description: The tool's registered name; never its arguments.

outcome.description: Refused is the shop saying no; failed is the tool breaking.

events.name: product_viewed
events.description: A shopper opened a product page. Only with analytics consent.

arrived_from.description: The page before this one, by kind; direct when there was none in this tab.

metrics.name: tendero.search.degraded
metrics.description: Searches answered without one of their AI stages, by stage.

stage.description: The stage that did not answer.

metrics.name: tendero.search.vector_projection.failed
metrics.description: Product changes the vector layer could not take; the lexical index took them.

metrics.name: tendero.outbox.lag
metrics.description: Seconds between an event being raised and processed.

metrics.name: tendero.search.requests
metrics.description: Searches answered, by who asked, through what, typed or browsed, and whether anything came back.

actor.kind.description: Agent for MCP and UCP, and for a principal carrying an agent id; human otherwise (ADR 0036).

surface.description: The route the request came through. WebMCP inherits the shopper's session, so to the server it is the web; its evidence is `webmcp_tool_invoked`.

mode.description: Query when text was typed; browse when it was not — a category page, a home-page row.

category.description: Whether the search was narrowed to a category.

result.description: Whether the first page had any product.

metrics.name: tendero.carts.created
metrics.description: Carts opened. Against placed orders, it is abandonment: nothing sets a cart to Abandoned yet, so the difference is the measure.

actor.kind.description: Agent for MCP and UCP, and for a principal carrying an agent id; human otherwise (ADR 0036).

surface.description: The route the request came through. WebMCP inherits the shopper's session, so to the server it is the web; its evidence is `webmcp_tool_invoked`.

metrics.name: tendero.checkout.attempts
metrics.description: Every place-order attempt by its outcome; orders placed are the ones whose outcome is placed.

actor.kind.description: Agent for MCP and UCP, and for a principal carrying an agent id; human otherwise (ADR 0036).

surface.description: The route the request came through. WebMCP inherits the shopper's session, so to the server it is the web; its evidence is `webmcp_tool_invoked`.

discounted.description: Whether any promotion applied to the order.

metrics.name: tendero.returns.requested
metrics.description: Lines of the returns opened, by their reason: the closed set of five the domain keeps for exactly this analysis.

metrics.name: tendero.catalog.products.published
metrics.description: Products moved from Draft to Active.

actor.kind.description: Agent for MCP and UCP, and for a principal carrying an agent id; human otherwise (ADR 0036).

metrics.name: tendero.inventory.reservations
metrics.description: Reservation transitions, by the state they reach.

status.description: ReservationStatus, labelled by MetricLabels. Expired is never recorded yet: nothing expires a hold.

metrics.name: tendero.agent.tool_calls
metrics.description: Calls from external agents to the MCP tools and the UCP catalogue operations.

surface.description: The binding the call came through.

tool.description: The tool or operation name; a closed set of the ones served.

outcome.description: Refused is the shop saying no; failed is the tool breaking.
